chunks: 4918 - Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:
There are three traits in one from whom no good is ever hoped: one who does not fear Allah in private, does not restrain himself in old age, and does not feel shame from fault.

key_terms.الشَّيْبِ: old age or greying with age
key_terms.الْغَيْبِ: privacy or what is hidden from people
key_terms.يَخْشَ: to fear Allah with reverence and God-consciousness
key_terms.يَرْعَوِ: to desist, be restrained, or take admonition

ai.seo_question: What qualities show that no good can be expected from a person?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام identifies three signs of deeply rooted moral failure: lack of God-consciousness in private, persistence in misconduct despite old age, and shamelessness regarding faults. The hadith stresses that true goodness depends on inner taqwa, moral restraint, and a living sense of shame before wrongdoing.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4918 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"There are three traits in a person from whom no good can ever be expected: one who does not fear Allah (swt) in private, one who shows no restraint in old age, and one who feels no shame from committing faults."
